description: Reads the animation parameters straight from the source file instead of measuring pixels: a Lottie file (.json or .lottie, a path or an http(s) link such as lottie.host), a Rive file (.riv, a path or a direct link to the .riv; rive.app pages are not read) or a Figma prototype link with node-id. Reports the composition, every move with its exact cubic-bezier curve, duration and values, the palette, fonts and text, and lists what could not be evaluated (expressions). Writes motion-spec.json and STYLE.md (plus RIVE.md with artboards, animations and state machines for Rive) to the workspace in the same shape as `style`, so the move data can feed the exporters. Figma links need FIGMA_TOKEN (a read-only personal access token). In Claude Code the official Figma MCP tool get_motion_context can also be used: pass its output here as `figma_json` and no token is needed. Pass `export` to also write a starter project (hyperframes, remotion, css, after-effects, lottie, hypit). A video or GIF has no animation data to read: measure it with `plan` or `style` instead.

export.description: Also write a starter project for this renderer.

figma_json.description: Figma JSON: a /v1/files/:key/nodes response or get_motion_context output. Use instead of `source`.

source.description: Path or http(s) link to a Lottie .json/.lottie or a Rive .riv file, or a figma.com link with node-id.

name: exact
title: Exact animation data (Lottie, Rive, Figma)
